annotations.annotation_text: Mamalujo signal "waves" on page 624 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): the Four Old Men — Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; Ulster, Munster, Leinster, Connaught — serve here as senile chroniclers and bedpost witnesses during dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea. In this Ricorso (The Return) passage, they observe and record the dream's events as squawking gulls circling overhead.
sources: O'Donovan, John. The Annals of the Four Masters. https://celt.ucc.ie/published/T100005A/
MacCabe, Colin. James Joyce and the Revolution of the Word. https://archive.org/details/jamesjoycerevolu0000macc
FWEET: Mamalujo / Four Old Men concordance. https://www.fweet.org
Ricorso.net: James Joyce Critical Archive. https://www.ricorso.net

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "pub" on page 624 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea. During this Ricorso (The Return) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
Gordon, John. Finnegans Blog (Tavern chapters). https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
